input.quote: 14.1 Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.
input.rationale: Section 14.1 is mutual and already contains an M&A/substantially-all-assets carve-out permitting assignment without consent, and there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right anywhere in the Agreement (no "change of control" trigger appears in the document, and Section 11 termination rights do not include one), so this is not walk-away territory. However, it falls short of the fallback on a material term: consent for all other assignments is left to the other party's absolute discretion, with no "not unreasonably withheld" standard, and there is no affiliate carve-out, so a routine internal reorganization by Corio could be blocked outright. The proposed edit is the minimum needed — it adds the reasonableness standard and an affiliate carve-out while preserving the existing mutual structure. The remaining gaps against the preferred position (the direct-competitor consent carve-back applies to Corio's transactions as well as Commerce One's, rather than only barring assignment to a Corio competitor) are noted but not pressed, given the balanced mutual bargain struck in this clause.

proposal.summary: Add reasonableness standard to assignment consent and an affiliate carve-out in Section 14.1
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a "not unreasonably withheld" standard to the consent requirement and a carve-out permitting assignment to affiliates, so an internal reorganization or entity migration cannot be blocked at the other party's discretion. This keeps Section 14.1 mutual and leaves the existing merger/acquisition carve-out and competitor exception intact.
